I'm examining those short "v"-shaped forked endings in the crops—small dark wedges about 4-6 units long with blunt arrowhead tips. I'm trying to trace which brush function produced them, considering candidates like the fine rigger twig strokes or clustered sub-shapes from the zigzag generator.

Looking at the full view, the oak crown reads as having too many visible "v" tips, which the critic compared to bird tracks—noticeable at the top and right edges but not egregious. Real oak silhouettes have dense, fine, gnarled twig haze at their edges rather than distinct blunt forks, so I'm planning to add a layer of very thin rigger strokes extending crookedly outward from the existing forks, breaking up the blunt v-shapes into joints and adding peripheral density—though I need to pick a color that reads as receding rather than the grey-whitish haze mix that failed before.

Since I don't have exact positions for all 155 twig tips, I'm considering approximating fork locations from the existing spray data and angles rather than trying to compute them precisely, and adding new finer growth starting near those approximate points rather than exactly at the known tips.

The deeper issue is that oak twigs cluster buds at their tips, so the blunt "v" shapes might be conceptually right but too uniform in size and crookedness — real oak twigs are short, zig-zagging, and bunch irregularly. I need to introduce real variety in length, angle, and bareness so the silhouette doesn't just repeat the same motif at a bigger scale, then test this with a trial sketch.

I should test on scratch paper first: paint a ground, draw a branch with a "v" ending like the current ones using a rigger, let it dry, then try finer tails with a thinner rigger at lighter pressure to compare results and judge which reads more convincingly as an oak twig tip. I also want to check how thin a mark the rigger can actually produce, and then systematically map out where the visible forks are across the crown using gridded crops so I can address them methodically.

I'm weighing whether to manually catalog roughly 70-150 fork tips by eye across the crop regions and give each a tail -- laborious but a legitimate painterly approach of looking and placing marks deliberately. An alternative would be approximating tails from estimated spray endpoints, though that feels less accurate; a middle path might be identifying regions and anchoring new fine twig systems on existing branch points within each.

I want to check the crown at full-view scale to judge how visible the v-shaped tips are at viewing distance -- the overview shows arrowhead-like v's at the top and right that seem worth fixing. I'm also considering the haze twigs: the glaze clipped to limb masks removes them on wood, but ones against the sky will get partially covered once I add dark fine tails and spurs, and I should verify the masks by checking the K value in the log.

rg_s = brush{kind="rigger", width=1.6, point=1}
rd_m = brush{kind="round", width=4, point=1}
function angular_pts(x, y, ang, len, nseg, jit, upb)
  local nodes = {{x, y, ang}}
  local a = ang
  local cx, cy = x, y
  for i=1,nseg do
    local seg = len/nseg * rand(0.7, 1.3)
    a = a + randn(0, jit)
    a = a + upb*((-math.pi/2) - a) + 0.3*(ang - a)
    cx, cy = cx + seg*math.cos(a), cy + seg*math.sin(a)
    nodes[#nodes+1] = {cx, cy, a}
  end
  return nodes
end
function draw_angular(br, nodes, w0, pl)
  local pts = {}
  local n = #nodes
  for i=1,n-1 do
    local a, b = nodes[i], nodes[i+1]
    for k=0,2 do
      local t = k/3
      local tt = ((i-1) + t)/(n-1)
      local w = w0*(1 - 0.75*tt)
      local p = math.max(0.3, br:pressure_for(math.max(w, 0.7)))
      pts[#pts+1] = {lerp(a[1], b[1], t), lerp(a[2], b[2], t), p}
    end
  end
  pts[#pts+1] = {nodes[n][1], nodes[n][2], 0.08}
  if br:fullness() < 0.45 then br:reload(pl, 0.75) end
  br:gesture(pts, {wobble=0.1, ramps={0.02, 0.25}})
end
function oak_spray(x, y, ang, len, w, depth, pl)
  local br = (w > 1.7) and rd_m or rg_s
  local nodes = angular_pts(x, y, ang, len, math.random(2, 3), 0.45, 0.1)
  draw_angular(br, nodes, w, pl)
  if depth > 0 then
    local tip = nodes[#nodes]
    local wc = math.max(0.8, w*0.62)
    oak_spray(tip[1], tip[2], tip[3] + randn(0, 0.25), len*rand(0.55, 0.8), wc, depth-1, pl)
    for j=1,math.random(1, 2) do
      local s = (math.random()<0.5) and -1 or 1
      oak_spray(tip[1], tip[2], tip[3] + s*rand(0.5, 1.0), len*rand(0.45, 0.7), wc, depth-1, pl)
    end
  end
end

tb = brush{kind="round", width=1.2, point=1}
tb:reload(t_twig, 0.7)
function seg_pts(pts_in, p0, p1)
  -- pts_in: polyline nodes; pressure falls p0 -> p1 along the length; densified to keep corners
  local L = 0
  for i=2,#pts_in do L = L + math.sqrt((pts_in[i][1]-pts_in[i-1][1])^2 + (pts_in[i][2]-pts_in[i-1][2])^2) end
  local out, acc = {}, 0
  for i=1,#pts_in-1 do
    local a, b = pts_in[i], pts_in[i+1]
    local d = math.sqrt((b[1]-a[1])^2 + (b[2]-a[2])^2)
    local n = math.max(2, math.floor(d/1.5))
    for k=0,n-1 do
      local t = k/n
      local s = (acc + d*t)/L
      out[#out+1] = {lerp(a[1], b[1], t), lerp(a[2], b[2], t), lerp(p0, p1, s^0.8)}
    end
    acc = acc + d
  end
  out[#out+1] = {pts_in[#pts_in][1], pts_in[#pts_in][2], p1}
  return out
end
function tail(x, y, a, len, bend, spur, p0)
  p0 = p0 or 0.55
  local bx, by = x - 1.5*math.cos(a), y - 1.5*math.sin(a)
  local l1 = len * rand(0.35, 0.5)
  local mx, my = x + l1*math.cos(a), y + l1*math.sin(a)
  local a2 = a + bend
  local l2 = len - l1
  local ex, ey = mx + l2*math.cos(a2), my + l2*math.sin(a2)
  if tb:fullness() < 0.4 then tb:reload(t_twig, 0.7) end
  tb:gesture(seg_pts({{bx,by},{x,y},{mx,my},{ex,ey}}, p0, 0.02), {wobble=0.03, ramps={0.02, 0.15}})
  if spur then
    local sa = a + spur
    local sl = rand(3, 5)
    tb:gesture(seg_pts({{mx,my},{mx + sl*math.cos(sa), my + sl*math.sin(sa)}}, 0.45, 0.02), {wobble=0.02, ramps={0.02, 0.2}})
  end
end

tb = brush{kind="round", width=1.2, point=1}
function seg_pts(pts_in, p0, p1)
  local L = 0
  for i=2,#pts_in do L = L + math.sqrt((pts_in[i][1]-pts_in[i-1][1])^2 + (pts_in[i][2]-pts_in[i-1][2])^2) end
  local out, acc = {}, 0
  for i=1,#pts_in-1 do
    local a, b = pts_in[i], pts_in[i+1]
    local d = math.sqrt((b[1]-a[1])^2 + (b[2]-a[2])^2)
    local n = math.max(2, math.floor(d/1.5))
    for k=0,n-1 do
      local t = k/n
      local s = (acc + d*t)/L
      out[#out+1] = {lerp(a[1], b[1], t), lerp(a[2], b[2], t), lerp(p0, p1, s^0.8)}
    end
    acc = acc + d
  end
  out[#out+1] = {pts_in[#pts_in][1], pts_in[#pts_in][2], p1}
  return out
end
-- tw: a fine crooked continuation from a prong end (x0,y0) toward (x1,y1)
-- bend: sideways offset of the elbow (units, + = to the right of travel); spur: nil or side (+1/-1) for a short near-right-angle spur at the elbow
function tw(x0, y0, x1, y1, bend, spur, pl, p0)
  pl = pl or t_twig; p0 = p0 or 0.65
  local dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
  local L = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
  local ux, uy = dx/L, dy/L
  local nx, ny = -uy, ux
  local bx, by = x0 - 1.3*ux, y0 - 1.3*uy
  local t = rand(0.35, 0.55)
  local ex, ey = x0 + dx*t + nx*bend, y0 + dy*t + ny*bend
  if tb:fullness() < 0.4 then tb:reload(pl, 0.7) end
  tb:gesture(seg_pts({{bx,by},{x0,y0},{ex,ey},{x1,y1}}, p0, 0.02), {wobble=0.03, ramps={0.02, 0.15}})
  if spur then
    local a = math.atan(y1 - ey, x1 - ex) + spur*rand(1.1, 1.45)
    local sl = rand(2.5, 5)
    tb:gesture(seg_pts({{ex,ey},{ex + sl*math.cos(a), ey + sl*math.sin(a)}}, 0.42, 0.02), {wobble=0.02, ramps={0.02, 0.2}})
  end
end
tb:reload(t_twig, 0.7)
print("ok")

-- crooked tapering shoot from (x,y) at angle a: 2-3 elbows, optional near-right-angle spur, fine point
function shoot(x, y, a, len, p0, pl, spur_p)
  pl = pl or t_twig; p0 = p0 or 0.6; spur_p = spur_p or 0.4
  local nseg = math.random(2, 3)
  local pts = {{x, y}}
  local cx, cy, ca = x, y, a
  local sgn = (math.random() < 0.5) and -1 or 1
  local elbows = {}
  for i=1,nseg do
    local seg = len/nseg * rand(0.7, 1.3)
    if i > 1 then ca = ca + sgn*rand(0.35, 0.7); sgn = -sgn end
    ca = ca + 0.12*((-math.pi/2) - ca)   -- slight upward pull
    cx, cy = cx + seg*math.cos(ca), cy + seg*math.sin(ca)
    pts[#pts+1] = {cx, cy}
    elbows[#elbows+1] = {cx, cy, ca}
  end
  if tb:fullness() < 0.4 then tb:reload(pl, 0.7) end
  tb:gesture(seg_pts(pts, p0, 0.02), {wobble=0.03, ramps={0.02, 0.15}})
  if math.random() < spur_p and #elbows >= 2 then
    local e = elbows[1]
    local s = (math.random() < 0.5) and -1 or 1

end
